rationale: A wins because it finds the tension inside the mechanics, not just the desks that might cover the announcement. "Perplexity is now paid twice on the same answer — and the publisher gets a slice of one payment" is risky, but it names a real economic question and then properly says "if it is shared, this angle dies"; B's closest version, "One AI app, two new ways to take a cut," is cleaner and flatter, like a strategy slide wearing a press badge. A has a bad overreach on "being sued," but its proof gates and uncomfortable questions would save a founder from making dumb calls.
gaps_in_A: "Perplexity starts paying publishers it was being sued over" overstates the record. The update says criticism and legal threats, not an active lawsuit.
"those same publishers" is not proven. No publisher is named as enrolled, and no former legal adversary is confirmed participating.

"Perplexity is now paid twice on the same answer" is a headline ahead of the facts. The set later admits the referral/ad-revenue relationship needs confirmation, which is good discipline, but the angle title still asserts too much.

"A multi-billion-dollar valuation now has two revenue lines to defend it" is the thinnest angle. Without revenue materiality, round details, or an investor on record, this is closer to a reported question than a story.
gaps_in_B: "One AI app, two new ways to take a cut" mostly repackages the shopping and publisher angles. It is defensible, but the distinct angle is mushier than the headline thinks.
"there is no story until a real number exists" throws away a useful accountability angle. The missing payout number is not just a blocker; it can be the story if framed as arithmetic and opacity.

"which merchants or product categories are live at launch; the referral-fee structure..." misses the sharper consumer-trust proof: whether product ranking is influenced by referral fees and how that is disclosed.

"What Perplexity's multi-billion valuation says about the AI bubble" is rightly refused, but B never rebuilds the narrower defensible version: whether these two revenue lines do any work against the valuation. That is a missed business-press angle, not a hallucination if handled carefully.
